title: Module 4: Application Forms
description: Forms, fields, lists, and views; client-side vs. server-side scripting; UI policies; client scripts; business rules and their execution order; the g_scratchpad object.

questions.prompt: Why should you choose a field's data type carefully when first creating it?

choices.text: The data type cannot be changed once any record exists.
Changing the type later can result in data loss.
The data type determines the field's column name.
Only the first field on a table is allowed to have a non-string type.

questions.explanation: Field types can be changed, but doing so after data exists can cause data loss, so the type should be chosen carefully up front. Use date/date-time fields for dates and reference/choice fields rather than free-form strings.

questions.prompt: You relabel a field that was originally defined on a parent table. What is the risk?

choices.text: The column name is renamed everywhere, breaking existing scripts.
The relabel can propagate to the parent table and its sibling tables.
The field is automatically deleted from the parent table.
All records in that column are cleared.

questions.explanation: Relabeling a parent-defined field can change the label on the parent and all sibling tables. Relabeling changes only the label (not the column name), and to scope a label change you should relabel on your own table.

questions.prompt: What happens to the data in a column's existing records when you delete a user-defined field from a table?

choices.text: The entire table records are deleted along with the column.
No table records are deleted; only the column is removed.
The records are archived to a recovery table.
The column is hidden but the data remains queryable.

questions.explanation: Deleting a field removes the column but does not delete any table records. Note also that inherited fields and system columns cannot be deleted, and in Table Builder you must clear a column's existing data before the column can be deleted.

questions.prompt: After creating a new field on a table, where does it appear automatically?

choices.text: On both the form's layout and in every single list view that exists for that table.
On the form's available fields (to drag onto the form), but not in any list view.
In all list views, but not on the form.
Nowhere; it must be added manually to both forms and lists.

questions.explanation: A new field is added to the form's available fields so it can be placed on the form, but it is not automatically added to a list view. You must personalize/configure the list layout to add the column.

questions.prompt: When do tabs appear on a form?

choices.text: Only when the form has one or more related lists attached at the bottom.
When the form has two or more sections (tabbed layout is the baseline).
Only when a developer explicitly enables them in the instance's system properties.
On every form, regardless of sections.

questions.explanation: Tabs appear when there are two or more sections, and tabbed layout is the platform's default/baseline. Users can switch to an accordion layout in their Display preferences. Tabs at the bottom of a form are related lists, not sections.

questions.prompt: Which method displays a message on a blue background directly below a specific field on a form?
questions.explanation: showFieldMsg() prints below the named field. addInfoMessage() (blue) and addErrorMessage() (red) print at the top of the form, and alert()/confirm() open JavaScript dialogs.

questions.prompt: What is a view in ServiceNow?

choices.text: A copy of a table's data for reporting.
A saved layout of a form or list defining which fields appear and in what order.
A role that grants read-only access.
A scheduled job that periodically refreshes cached form layouts.

questions.explanation: A view is a saved layout of a form or list. It lets the same record be displayed in different ways for different audiences (for example ESS, ITIL, mobile).

questions.prompt: A view has the database Name "ess" but is shown to users as "Self Service". What is "Self Service" in this case?

choices.text: The name of the role a user must hold in order to see the view.
The table the view applies to.
The column name the view sorts by.

questions.explanation: Every view has a Name (database name, here "ess") and a Title (the friendly name shown to users, here "Self Service").

questions.prompt: Which role does a user need in order to change the view they are seeing?
questions.explanation: The view_changer role is required for a user to switch the view they see. Not all users have permission to change views.

questions.prompt: What makes a View Rule different from forcing a view via a module configuration or a URL parameter?

choices.text: A View Rule applies only to list views and never to forms in any circumstance whatsoever.
A View Rule forces the view from the server and can't be overridden by URL query strings.
A View Rule can only ever use the condition builder to match records, and never any custom script.
A View Rule runs on the client and is therefore faster.

questions.explanation: View Rules force a view from the server-side and cannot be fooled by injecting query strings into the URL, unlike views set via a module or a URL parameter.

questions.prompt: In a scripted View Rule, how do you specify which view to force?

choices.text: Return the view's friendly Title string directly from the view rule script.
Set the variable named "answer" to the system name of the view.
Call g_form.setView() with the view name.
Set current.view to the desired view.

questions.explanation: In a scripted view rule you set the answer variable to the system Name of the view you want to force. Server-side JavaScript lets you check role/group membership, and a switch/case block handles complex situations.

questions.prompt: Which three field attributes are UI Policies specifically designed to toggle?
questions.explanation: UI Policy Actions toggle whether a field is mandatory, visible, and/or read-only (and can optionally clear the field value).

questions.prompt: A UI Policy's condition is NOT re-evaluated when a field value changes through which of the following?

choices.text: A user manually changing a field on the form.
An onChange that updates a field the user typed in.
An Import Set, web service, UI Action, or the List Editor.
A user editing the field and tabbing out.

questions.explanation: UI Policy conditions are only re-checked when a user manually changes a field on a form. Changes made via UI Action, context menu, Import Set, web services, or the List Editor do not re-evaluate them. To enforce mandatory/read-only for non-form changes, use Data Policies (which are not scriptable).

questions.prompt: In a UI Policy, what must be enabled for the "Execute if false" script to run?

choices.text: The Global checkbox on the policy.
The Inherit from parent checkbox option.
The On load form trigger option.

questions.explanation: The Execute if false script only runs when "Reverse if false" is selected. The platform can't infer the inverse of arbitrary script, which is why separate true/false scripts (and this toggle) exist.

questions.prompt: A UI Policy can hide an entire form section, but a UI Policy Action cannot. What enables hiding a section?

choices.text: Setting the form section's container field itself to read-only on load.
Scripting in the UI Policy's advanced view (Run scripts).
The Order field on the UI Policy record itself controls this.

questions.explanation: UI Policy Actions can hide individual fields but not sections. Hiding/showing a whole section requires scripting in the UI Policy's advanced view.

questions.prompt: Which client script type fires when a record is submitted/saved?
questions.explanation: onSubmit() fires on submit/save, onLoad() when the form loads, onChange() when a specified field changes, and onCellEdit() from a list.

questions.prompt: Which client script type executes from a list rather than a form?
questions.explanation: onCellEdit() is the client script type that runs from a list (when a cell is edited). The other three run on forms.

questions.prompt: Client scripts and UI policies both run client-side. Which capabilities belong ONLY to client scripts (not UI policies)? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Access to a field's prior value.
Execute on a list field value change (onCellEdit).

questions.explanation: Only client scripts run on submit, can access a field's prior value, and run from a list. The Condition Builder belongs to UI policies, which also resolve after client scripts and require no scripting.

questions.prompt: Which two client-side classes are auto-instantiated for managing forms and the current user?
questions.explanation: g_form (GlideForm) manages form fields/values and g_user (GlideUser) exposes current-user info and role checks. Both are client-side and auto-instantiated; GlideSystem (gs) is server-side.

questions.prompt: Scoped client scripts are wrapped in an IIFE, blocking some APIs. Which API can NEVER be re-enabled, even by setting glide.script.block.client.globals to false?
questions.explanation: Setting glide.script.block.client.globals to false can re-enable blocked APIs except client-side GlideRecord, which can never be turned back on. Use GlideAjax instead for server lookups from the client.

questions.prompt: From a scoped client script you need data from another table. GlideRecord is blocked client-side. What is the recommended replacement?

choices.text: A jQuery AJAX request sent directly to a REST endpoint
Calling GlideSystem (gs) directly on the client side
Using only g_form.getReference() to fetch the data

questions.explanation: GlideAjax is the supported way to reach the server from a client script when client-side GlideRecord is unavailable. Server-side queries should run in server scripts.

questions.prompt: On a Business Rule record, on what does a Business Rule trigger?

choices.text: A user clicking a UI widget or button.

questions.explanation: Business Rules are server-side automation that run in response to database access (insert/update/delete/query), at before/after/display/async timing. Schedules trigger Scheduled Jobs, events trigger Script Actions, and widget clicks trigger UI Actions.

questions.prompt: What is the correct execution order of business rule types?
questions.explanation: Order: Query (as the query runs), Display (as the form renders, before onLoad client scripts), Before (after submit, before the write), After (after the write), Async (in the background like a scheduled job).

questions.prompt: Which business rule type runs as the form begins to render, before any onLoad client scripts fire, to make extra server data available?
questions.explanation: A Display Business Rule fires as the form renders, before onLoad client scripts, and its purpose is to populate the g_scratchpad object with data the form wouldn't otherwise carry.

questions.prompt: Which business rule type is best suited to validating a record and rejecting it before it is written to the database?
questions.explanation: A Before Business Rule runs after submit but before the record is written, which makes it ideal for validation (for example, aborting when an end date precedes a start date).

questions.prompt: You need to update records on a different table after a new record is successfully saved. Which business rule type fits best?
questions.explanation: An After Business Rule runs once the record is saved on the server, making it well suited to propagating values to or updating other records/tables. For long-running work that shouldn't block the user, an Async rule is preferable.

questions.prompt: Which business rule type behaves like a scheduled job, running in the background so it doesn't delay returning control to the user?
questions.explanation: An Async Business Rule runs in parallel in the background when the server gets to it, similar to a scheduled job. It suits slow work like web-service integrations. The other four types are synchronous.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the g_scratchpad object are correct? (Choose 2)

choices.text: It is populated by a Display Business Rule and read by client-side scripts.
All property values must be passed as strings.
It comes pre-populated with the record's field values by default.
It is fully supported on the mobile platform.

questions.explanation: g_scratchpad carries data from a Display Business Rule to client-side scripts, and its values must be strings. It has no properties by default and does not exist on the mobile platform.

questions.prompt: Why does impersonating another user affect the result of a g_user call in a client script?

choices.text: g_user permanently caches the original admin user's roles in the browser session.
g_user executes client-side and reflects the impersonated session's user.
g_user may only ever be invoked by users who currently hold the admin role.
Impersonation rewrites the server-side GlideSystem (gs) object and its role cache.

questions.explanation: Because g_user runs client-side and reflects the current (impersonated) session, role and identity checks return the impersonated user's values.

questions.prompt: On a script record, what is the Messages field used for?

choices.text: Documentation of who wrote the script and why.
Localization, matching keys against the sys_ui_message table.

questions.explanation: The Messages field supports localization: strings listed there are matched by key in sys_ui_message and replaced with a localized version when one exists. The Description field is for documentation, and the trigger defines when the script runs.

questions.prompt: Which classes are NOT available in server-side scripts because they are part of the client-side API?
questions.explanation: GlideForm (g_form) and GlideUser (g_user) are client-side and not available server-side. Server scripts use classes like GlideSystem (gs).

questions.prompt: Of the following script types, which one does NOT always run on the server?
questions.explanation: A UI Action can execute on the client or on the server depending on how it is configured, for example when the Client checkbox is set and an onclick function runs in the browser. Business Rules, Script Includes, and Script Actions always execute server-side.

questions.prompt: A GlideRecord query needs to match records where priority is 1 OR priority is 2. How is the OR condition added?

choices.text: Capture the object returned by addQuery() and call addOrCondition() on it.
Call addOrQuery() with both field values as arguments.
Call addQuery() twice; multiple addQuery() calls are automatically OR'd.
Pass an array of values to addQuery() to broaden the match.

questions.explanation: addQuery() returns a GlideQueryCondition, and calling addOrCondition() on that object ORs an alternative value into the query. There is no addOrQuery() method. Successive addQuery() calls are AND'd together, not OR'd, so calling it twice would require both conditions to be true.

questions.prompt: Which variables are NOT guaranteed to be available in every Business Rule? (Choose 2.)
questions.explanation: previous is not populated on insert operations because there is no prior version of the record, so it is not always available. g_scratchpad exists only to pass data from a Display Business Rule to client scripts, so it is not present in other Business Rules. The current record and the GlideSystem object are available in all Business Rules.

questions.prompt: When configuring an Async Business Rule, which database operation is NOT available as a trigger?
questions.explanation: An Async Business Rule can be triggered on Insert, Update, or Delete, but not on Query. Async rules are scheduled to run after the database transaction completes, so there is no read-time (Query) trigger for them, unlike a synchronous before/after rule.

questions.prompt: Which client-side method displays a message directly beneath a specific field on a form?
questions.explanation: The method that attaches a message to an individual field is showFieldMsg() (paired with hideFieldMsg()), abbreviated as Msg. The form-level banner methods addInfoMessage() and addErrorMessage() spell out Message and appear at the top of the form rather than under a field. A showFieldMessage() method does not exist.

questions.prompt: Which pair of Business Rule actions can be configured WITHOUT writing a script?

choices.text: Set field values and add a message.
Set field values and generate an event.
Set field values and write to the system log.
Set field values and query the database.

questions.explanation: The declarative Business Rule actions are Set field values (to a value, same as another field, or dynamically) and Add message, which posts text at the top of the page. Generating an event, writing to the log, or running a query all require code in the Script field.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a method of the client-side GlideUser (g_user) object?
questions.explanation: userName is a property accessed as g_user.userName, so there is no userName() method. hasRole(), hasRoleExactly(), and getFullName() are all real methods. getFullName() is a method because it computes a value (first plus last name) rather than exposing a stored attribute.

questions.prompt: On the client side, how do you read the sys_id of the currently logged-in user, and how does that differ from the server side?

choices.text: g_user.userID is a property on the client; gs.getUserID() is a method on the server.
g_user.getUserID() is a method on the client; gs.userID is a property on the server.
g_user.userID() is a method on both the client and the server.
gs.getUserID() works on both the client and the server.

questions.explanation: Client-side, the user's sys_id is exposed as the property g_user.userID (no parentheses). Server-side, it is returned by the method gs.getUserID(). The client identity values (userName, userID, firstName, lastName) are bare properties, while the server GlideSystem equivalents are method calls.
